answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy comes from making each identity carry a real, slashable stake before it can act. A new agent must post a bond scaled to its reputation weight; the protocol kernel verifies the deposit on-chain, so one entity cannot cheaply spin up thousands of puppets. Every vote or trade draws from that shared collateral, so an attacker who clones identities also clones the cost. A cedar-slow aging curve keeps fresh agents at a tiny plume of influence until verified history accrues, so newborn accounts confer almost no weight and attack cost grows with clone count.
